correctness.rationale: A full proper coloring of K_{n1,...,nr} with r+1 labelled colors has r disjoint nonempty part palettes, so either every part is monochromatic (one unused color), or exactly one part j has two colors, and all others are monochromatic. In the first case every blank sees at most r−1 neighbor colors forever, so forcing implies a total initial coloring. In the second case every vertex of the split part sees at most r−1 external colors and thus must be seeded; if >=2 nonsplit parts are completely blank, no first force sees r colors. Conversely, a fully seeded split part with both colors, all other parts seeded except at most one, forces the missing part then forces all remaining blanks. The r+1 colors can be chosen as an unordered pair for j and bijection on other parts in (r+1)!/2 ways; surjective two-color assignments on j number 2^{n_j}−2, and nonempty/blank seed choices give the exact H_G coefficient factor. Independent vertex weighting p,q gives FC. The minimum seed domain m+r−2 and its multiplicity follow by taking one blank nonsplit part and one selected vertex from every other nonsplit part. The all-singleton case is r! times choice of unused color. An independently written exhaustive enumerator verified all states for seven profiles (r=3 or 4 and singleton boundary), 89,557 initial assignments total, with exact polynomial coefficients and minimum counts. The universal theorem rests on the analytic dichotomy, not the finite checks.

originality.rationale: The exact all-profile r>=3 one-spare-palette formula and split-part characterization were compared against the 2024 primary definition, the published complete-multipartite λ=r theorem, the published bipartite λ=3 theorem, and maximum-degree-two results. The 2024 source gives only the general forcing indicator sum and a stall criterion. The two strongest later records cover complementary boundary cases; neither directly proves the new all-r condition or all-coefficient polynomial. Three semantic Resultary searches and targeted open literature searches found no decisive covering statement. The 2026 Farr preprint full text could not be independently retrieved in this run; that substantial uncertainty is expressly retained rather than pretending full-text exclusion.

value.rationale: The first color count above the chromatic number is a natural threshold in Farr’s recently introduced forced-colouring invariant. For arbitrary r>=3 and arbitrary positive part sizes, the exact successful-seed classification changes qualitatively from λ=r: propagation requires a wholly seeded two-color part and all but at most one other part seeded. This yields every coefficient, a probability polynomial and exact extremal seed number/count; it gives a benchmark for a natural graph class with unbounded sizes. Though the proof uses elementary counting and parallels the r=2 boundary, the complete r>=3 λ=r+1 invariant is not mechanically obtained by direct specialization of the inspected prior theorems. The result does not address larger palettes or arbitrary graphs.

final_claim: For every finite K_{n1,...,nr}, r>=3, positive n_i, with r+1 labelled colors, all forcing partial proper assignments are either completely seeded monochromatic r-part colorings, or have a unique fully seeded bicolored part j and all but at most one other part seeded in its singleton eventual color. The generating polynomial H_G, probability FC_{r+1}(G;p), minimum domain m+r-2 (when a non-singleton part exists), and minimum coefficient are as in RESULT.md.
limitations: Only r>=3 and exactly λ=r+1; singleton parts allowed. The r=2 case is prior and the all-singleton case trivial.
No general result for λ>=r+2 or for nonmultipartite graphs.
Independent verification covers seven finite profiles, not the infinite family; analytic argument supplies universality.
